Curse of the Law

precepts.text: Our forefathers that came up out of Egypt said Amen to this. We agreed to the covenant and to everything written in it.
precepts.point: If we do not apply his laws, all these curses shall come upon us and overtake us. That is how bad our condition got when God turned his back on us.

note.label: You Are Hated And In Hell

precepts.text: Cursed be he that maketh a graven image, dishonours his parents, removes the landmark, lies with a beast or his sister, takes reward to slay the innocent, and cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law; all the people said amen. Moral law, loving thy neighbour, agreed to on pain of death, and that is where Galatians 3:10 quotes from.
precepts.point: The just shall live by faith, from Habakkuk; the law is not of faith but the promise predates the law and sacrifice; and Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Galatians 3:10 says, “For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.” Deuteronomy 27 is where Paul is quoting from.

“Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.” That is death, and we agreed to it: break these commandments and we would be destroyed. Then it goes down the list. “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother”, that is, dishonours them. Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour's landmark, that maketh the blind to wander, that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow, that lieth with his father's wife. “Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast”: no animal atones for that. Cursed be he that lieth with his sister or his mother in law, that smiteth his neighbour secretly, that “taketh reward to slay an innocent person.” And every time, all the people said Amen. They agreed to being cursed if they violated these laws.

Then the last: “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.” That is the line Paul quotes. All these things go into morality, civil and moral law, dealing with your brother, your father, your sister; it goes right back to loving thy neighbour as thyself.

That is the curse. Idolatry, adultery, murder, bestiality: there was no repentance and no animal in the temple that could atone for them. The Galatians, the northern kingdom and the scattered Israelites, were heavily rooted in idolatry, so under the old covenant they were immediately condemned. That is why Paul asks whether they received the Spirit by the works of the law. If you are under that law of sacrifice, you are under the curse, because what you are guilty of cannot be atoned for under Mosaic law. They came into the faith hearing that Christ had died for them and redeemed them from sins the animals could never cover.

precepts.text: Cursed be the man that maketh any graven image, that setteth light by his father or mother, that removeth his neighbour's landmark, that maketh the blind to wander, that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, that lieth with his father's wife, with any manner of beast, with his sister, with his mother in law, that smiteth his neighbour secretly, that taketh reward to slay an innocent person, and cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them; and all the people shall say, Amen. We all agreed, and none of these can be atoned with an animal: it is death all throughout. The white man removed the landmarks of America, Africa, and Australia and cannot atone while he sits on the stolen land.
precepts.point: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. The lynchings of our people from trees, lamps, and bridges were not coincidental. Christ nailed to a wooden cross hung by his hands and feet for hours: that is a lynching, and Christ died a black man's death. That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse.” The works of the law, in Galatians 3:2, 3:5, 3:10 and 2:16, is sacrifice, as in Nehemiah 10:33. Under the curse means under the curse of the covenant. And “Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them” is Paul quoting Deuteronomy 27.

What does that curse mean? “Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image”, “And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.” Can he atone for it, reconcile with God, find justification? What animal can he use? None. Under the old covenant you get death. That is what cursed means.

So it goes all the way down. “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother”: disrespects, curses or strikes them. “Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour’s landmark.” The so-called white man has removed the neighbor's landmark: America is a stolen landmark, Africa is a stolen landmark, Australia is a stolen landmark. How can he atone when the land is still in his possession? He can't; he sits on stolen land. “Cursed be he that lieth with his father’s wife”, his stepmother. “Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast.” “Cursed be he that lieth with his sister”, “with his mother in law.” “Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly”: kills his brother secretly and does not get caught. “Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person”: a hitman, a mercenary.

After each one, “all the people shall say, Amen”: we all agreed to it. Then “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them”, which is exactly what Paul quotes. None of these could be atoned for with an animal. It is death all throughout.

That is why those of the works of the law are under the curse. We confirmed to do everything under that covenant of sacrifices, and if you violate a law that no animal can cover, you get the curse, which is death.

precepts.text: Thou shalt therefore obey the voice of the Lord thy God, and do his commandments and his statutes; that is what the voice of God tells a man to do.
precepts.point: For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt therefore obey the voice of the Lord thy God, and do his commandments and his statutes, which I command thee this day.” That is what the voice of God tells a man to do: keep his commandments.

So when it says “if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice”, that voice tells you to keep his commandments. If someone claims God spoke to him in a dream and told him everything but obedience, that is not the voice of the Most High.

precepts.text: Judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger; ye shall not respect persons in judgment.
precepts.point: This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

precepts.why:
“Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow.” This curse goes back to the beginning of Deuteronomy, where Moses charged the judges of Israel: “Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.” The stranger that dwells with Israel is to have righteous judgment the same as an Israelite.

“Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s”. A judge is not to be swayed by who stands before him, great or small, and not to fear any man's face, because the judgment belongs to the Most High. To pervert the judgment of the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, the ones with nobody to stand up for them, is to respect persons, the very thing the judges were charged never to do. That is why the curse falls on it, and all the people say Amen.

precepts.text: The nakedness of thy sister thou shalt not uncover; the curse repeats the law already given.
precepts.point: This goes back to Leviticus chapter 18, where the nakedness laws were first given.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

precepts.why:
“Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother.” This is not a new law spoken on the mount; it goes back to Leviticus 18, where the nakedness laws were first given: “The nakedness of thy sister, the daughter of thy father, or daughter of thy mother, whether she be born at home, or born abroad, even their nakedness thou shalt not uncover.”

The curse repeats the law already given. Whether the sister is born at home or born abroad, of the same father or of the same mother, her nakedness is not to be uncovered. The man who does it is cursed, and all the people say Amen.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God; the animal no longer suffices, the sacrifice is your body.
precepts.point: Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

precepts.why:
“Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them.” At the time it was spoken, that encompassed everything, the law of sacrifice included. It applies to us today as well, because sacrifice is alive and well; it just transformed. We still sacrifice, only it is no longer animals: it is our bodies.

Paul says it: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” The animal no longer suffices; the sacrifice is your body. And the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord, so our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. That is how confirming all the words of this law to do them reaches into our day.

precepts.text: He will magnify the law and make it honourable; Christ magnified the law, he did not do away with the sacrifice principle.
precepts.point: Our bodies must be holy and without blemish before the Most High, because the law says you cannot bring anything with blemishes into the house of the Lord. If your sacrifice is not holy and acceptable, the Son is not taking you to present you before the Father. Christ magnified the law, as Isaiah says.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

precepts.why:
“The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable.” Christ magnified the law. He did not do away with it, and he did not do away with the sacrifice principle; he made it honourable.

So the curse on him “that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them” still stands for us. The sacrifice transformed from the animal to our own bodies, presented holy and acceptable unto God, but the law itself was magnified, not removed. If your sacrifice is not holy, the Son is not presenting you before the Father.

precepts.text: Cursed is he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, and cursed is he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person.
precepts.point: David set this man up to get murdered, and Israel does this too, contrary to popular belief. This goes back to Deuteronomy 27: cursed is he that smiteth his neighbour secretly, because nobody knew what David was doing, and cursed is he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. The reward was that woman; he slew an innocent man who had done nothing.

note.label: 2 Samuel 11: David, Bathsheba, and the Murder of Uriah

precepts.why:
“Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen. Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person.”

David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah himself: “Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.” Joab assigned him to a place where he knew valiant men were, “and Uriah the Hittite died also.”

David set this man up to get murdered, and Israel does this too, contrary to popular belief. He smote his neighbour secretly, because nobody knew what David was doing. And he took reward to slay an innocent person: the reward was that woman, and he slew an innocent man who had done nothing. Both curses fall on this deed.

precepts.text: Cursed is the man that maketh a graven or molten image and putteth it in a secret place, a hidden thing worshipped in secret.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 3: Solomon Builds the Temple

precepts.why:
“Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and putteth it in a secret place.” The curse falls on the image made and put in a secret place, a hidden thing worshipped in secret.

A wall in a man’s house is not a secret place. It is seen plainly when a man enters the home; it is not hidden. Solomon’s cherubims were graved on the walls of the house of the Lord, open for all to see, not hidden away to be worshipped in the dark.

precepts.text: Cursed be he that sets light by his father or his mother.
precepts.point: Say not thou I will recompense evil, but wait on the Lord and he shall save thee. When Absalom and Ahithophel conspired against David, he did not go physically to destroy them but prayed and fasted and waited for the Lord's answer.

note.label: Proverbs 20: Integrity, Just Weights, and Waiting on the Lord

precepts.why:
“Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness.” The law says the same in the curses spoken from the mount: “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen.”

To set light by your father or mother, to make little of them, is to fall under a curse all Israel answered Amen to. Solomon's lamp put out in obscure darkness is that curse: the man who curses his parents is himself cursed.

It stands beside the stubborn and rebellious son who is brought before the elders. Cursing father and mother carries both the judgment of the elders and the curse of the whole congregation.

precepts.text: Cursed is everyone that confirms not all the words of this law to do them.
precepts.point: Hear the words of this covenant: cursed be the man that obeys not its words.

note.label: Jeremiah 11: The Broken Covenant

precepts.why:
The curse Jeremiah is told to speak to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem is the curse of the law itself. Moses had already said it: “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.” Our fathers answered Amen to it.

So when the Lord says “Cursed be the man that obeyeth not the words of this covenant”, he is holding Israel to the very words they agreed to. The covenant is the law, and the curse is on everyone that confirms not all of its words to do them.

precepts.text: Cursed is he that confirmeth not all the words of this law, a curse commanded to the people of Israel.
precepts.point: The purpose is that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern tribes, through Christ, who redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel. "All nations blessed in Abraham" means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.”

This is the curse of the law, and it was commanded to the people of Israel. They are the ones who said Amen to it. So the ones Christ redeemed from the curse of the law are Israel.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 6 The 4 Horsemen

precepts.why: This explains the two mountains. “These shall stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people, when ye are come over Jordan; Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Joseph, and Benjamin: And these shall stand upon mount Ebal to curse; Reuben, Gad, and Asher, and Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.” When we went in the wilderness there were two huge mountains, and God split Israel up. He said these tribes go on this mountain to send forth the blessings, and the rest of you tribes go on the other mountain and you bring forth the curses that come if you break God's commandments.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 22
